testIdRule: Non-departmental: occurrences 1–12 Mid 1, 13–24 Mid 2, 25–36 ESE. Departmental: occurrences 1–12 Mid 1, 13–24 Mid 2.
notes: Exact normalized subject-name matches with the same departmental flag are reused verbatim even if syllabus descriptions differ, per user instruction.

For non-name matches, reuse still requires departmental-flag and unit/topic alignment. An exact-name match with an incompatible departmental flag raises an error rather than silently generating a replacement bank.
Mid 1 scope is recorded from the first half of the ordered syllabus units; confirm against the official exam blueprint.
Generated question pools and theory answers are drafts requiring academic review.
TestsData contains only TestId, Questions, Options and Answers; mappings are held in test_index.
Theory rows use Options=[] and model answers in Answers; consumers must explicitly support both formats.
Project subjects are excluded completely and have no exam type banks or TestIds.
Compatible exact-name duplicates reuse source payloads verbatim.
New question pools and model answers are deterministic template-generated drafts requiring academic QA before production.

subjects.name: Digital Logic and Design
subjects.objective: The subject aims to prepare the students,  To understand the basic of Digital Electronic concepts required in analysis and design of digital electronic circuits and systems.  To understand the number system, logic gates, Boolean algebra, etc.  To understand Construction and operation of various digital circuits such as Adder, Subtractor, Multiplexer, Demultiplexer, Decoder, Encoder, Flip-flops, Counters Registers.  To devolve the capability to Simplify, Analyze Various Digital Electronic Circuits. Credits Earned: 3 Credits
course_outcomes: After completion of this course, student will be able to  Perform conversion between various number systems.  Apply knowledge of Boolean algebra and other minimization techniques for digital circuit design.  Identify, formulate and solve a problem based on combinational and sequential circuits  Select the appropriate hardware and software tools for combinational and sequential circuit design.  Design various counters.  Verify the functions of various digital integrated circuits.  Evaluate the specifications of logic families.  Create a course project using digital integrated circuits.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction: 1
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Digital and Analog systems, logic level and pulse waveforms, elements of digital logic, Functions of digital logic

allSyllabusUnits.title: Number systems and binary codes : 6
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Number System: Binary number system (addition, subtraction, multiplication, Division), Octal and Hexadecimal Number system, Conversion from binary to decimal, octal and hexadecimal and vice versa, Representation of Signed Numbers. Codes : BCD, XS-3, Gray Code ( with Conversion), Alphanumerical Code

allSyllabusUnits.title: Logic Gates & Boolean Algebra 7
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Logic Gates: Positive and Negative logic, AND, OR , NOT, NAND, NOR, X-OR Gate, X-NOR Gate ( all gates with symbol, working principal and truth table), Conversion from Universal Gate to all other Gates, Boolean Algebra & Mapping Methods for Simplification: Boolean Algebra, Karnaugh Maps, Realizing Logic Function with Gates.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Combinational logic design: 7.5
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Combinational Circuits and its implementations, Arithmetic Circuits - Adders and Subtractor, BCD Adder, Look-Ahead Carry Generator, Multiplier, Magnitude comparator. Multiplexer and it’s application, Encoders, Demultiplexers and Decoders and it’s application, Parity Generation and Checking, Code Conversion.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Sequential circuits: 5
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Flip-flops: Latch and Flip-flop, S-R flip-flops, D flip flop, J-K flip flop, Application of flip flops Registers: Classification , Serial in serial-out, serial-in parallel-out, parallel- in serial-out and parallel-in parallel out shift register Counters: Asynchronous (ripple) 4-bit binary counter, BCD Counter, Synchronous counters, UP/DOWN counter, Ring counters.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Programmable Devices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: 1.5 Introduction to Programmable Logic Devices, Programmable Logic Arrays Syllabus for Diploma Engineering Information and Communication Technology (PLA), Programmable Array Logic (PAL). TOTAL HOURS 28 100

subjects.name: ICT Workshop
subjects.objective: This course deals with basic introduction of system components of electronic systems, and provides hands on practice in assembling, interconnecting, testing, and repairing such system by making use of various tools. Also, this course will provide ​a much needed knowledge of computer hardware and networking, enabling them to identify and rectify the onboard computer hardware, software and network related problems. With the help of this course the student will be able to understand the hardware specifications that are required to run operating system and various application programs. Credits Earned: ​3 Credits
course_outcomes: ​After completion of this course, student will be able to 1. Understand Basic Computer components and tools. 2. The students will apply knowledge of engineering to design and conduct experiments using PCB design software. 3. Identify the existing configuration of the computers and peripherals. 4. Apply their knowledge about computer peripherals to identify / rectify problems onboard. 5. Integrate the PCs into local area network and re-install operating system and various application programs.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction and Assembling of computer 8
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Basics of computer modules, Assembling various computer parts like Processor (CPU), Computer Case, Optical Drives, Memory, Power Supply, Motherboard, Processor Fan, Case Fan

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction to various network components 10
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Understanding Network Components like Routers, Hubs, Switch, Bridge, Gateways, NICs, Wireless Access Points, Modems

allSyllabusUnits.title: PCB Design Process 13
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Conception Level Introduction: Specifying Parts, Packages and Pin Names, Libraries and Checking foot prints of the components, Partlist, Placing Parts, Routing Traces, Modifying Traces, Mounting Holes, Adding Text, PCB Layout, Pattern Transfer.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Installation of operating system 10
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to Operating systems, Step wise process to install Operating Systems

allSyllabusUnits.title: Establishment of local area network and implementation of file 12
allSyllabusUnits.topics: sharing on network Understanding basic Network Topologies, Cramping of LAN, Setting up connections between PCs, File Transferring and Sharing

allSyllabusUnits.title: User Centric Applications using open source boards and IDE 17
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Various boards, hardware specifications, components and various pins, connection with hardware and libraries, ​Program structure, use of built in functions and use define functions, implementation of project TOTAL HOURS 70 100 Marwadi University Faculty of Diploma studies Information and Communication Technology
